title: Native fallback must stay type-consistent with to_arrow_field and Arrow path
answers: DateTime64 nanoseconds lost in ClickHouse native sync
How are ClickHouse Native values converted to Arrow
Why are JSON(...) and Dynamic(...) columns wrapped in toString
body:
The Native fallback in clickhouse.py must produce batches matching `pa.schema([c.to_arrow_field() ...])`.
- `DateTime64` columns are requested with `column_formats={name: "int"}` and converted by `_ticks_to_timestamp`, because Python datetimes truncate to microseconds and DateTime64(7..9) would lose digits.
- `_native_column_to_arrow` stringifies values (`str()`) when the target field is string but Native decodes tuples/lists (geo types, AggregateFunction); other type errors re-raise.
- Types the Arrow path can't handle are wrapped in `toString()` by `_build_select_list` using the prefix tuple (now including `"JSON("` and `"Dynamic("`), applied on both paths; add new unsupported parameterized types there.
Known accepted divergence: DateTime is uint32 on Arrow path vs timestamp[s] on Native.
applies: ClickHouse source column typing in both Arrow and Native paths
